title: The Chaos Isn't Necessary
summary: Four years in: the sense of chaos in marketing compliance work isn't necessary. A note from Blee's head of marketing on the new site and what's underneath.
body_markdown:
Listen, I’m a marketer so I know the jokes–this isn’t brain surgery, we’re not saving lives, and yet, I also know that usually everything feels like an emergency. The launch is tomorrow. The font is wrong (and yes, they will notice if you ask a designer!). The script didn't get approved. The influencer post went live with the wrong disclosure. The CMO wants to know why a campaign that was supposed to go out Monday is still in review.


Here's the part I've learned over the last year talking to the legal and compliance leaders Blee works with: It feels exactly the same on that side, too. The queue is full. The asset count keeps climbing. Marketing is asking why something is taking two weeks. You're trying to apply genuine scrutiny to fifty pieces a day that, four years ago, would have been five.


Both sides feel like they're behind. Both sides feel like they're letting someone down. Both sides have been told to move faster.


We've come to believe this sense of chaos frankly isn't necessary. What you need—what we have all needed for a long time—is control and calm.


That's the thing we've been building toward, one customer at a time, since 2022. Not in a single release. Not in a pivot. In the kind of purposeful, methodical accumulation that doesn't make for splashy launch announcements but, looking back, adds up to a different kind of product.


In the last six months I’ve seen a few examples of what that looked like in practice:


Our monitoring feature didn't come from a roadmap brainstorm. It came from one customer telling us, in pretty specific terms, what was slipping past their formal review process and how much time they were losing trying to manually catch it. They had to just “hope” that someone saw a social post or website update that broke a rule, and then had the wherewithal to mention it to legal so it could be addressed.That conversation became a feature. It's now one of the things customers most want to hear about when they come to us—not because we predicted it would be, but because we built it for someone real.


Our approval workflow has Guy's fingerprints on it. He was at Adobe before Blee, and saw the wave of AI-generated marketing content coming before most of the industry had a vocabulary for it. He's also the one who likes to say: *People come for the AI. They stay for the workflow.* And he means it. What's in the product today was shaped just as much by engineers and customers telling us, over and over, what *actually* breaks down in a real review queue. Where the bottlenecks are. Which tools your teams already live in. Why an integration in Figma matters more than an integration almost anywhere else.


That kind of building doesn't lend itself to a dramatic before-and-after. It's more like watching a house get built room by room. But after four years, the house is here. And it doesn't look like the rest of the neighborhood.


Which brings me to the new site.


When you land on it, you'll see a mountain landscape at golden hour. Wildflowers. A serif headline that reads *From top of mind. To peace of mind.* You will not see what most software in our category shows you—the urgency-coded dashboard, the red alerts, the breathless pitch about how fast we move.


That's a deliberate choice. The whole category sells legal and compliance teams more of what they already have too much of: urgency, alarm, the feeling of being behind. We don't think that's what serious oversight should feel like. We think it should feel like a tool that lets you actually rest at the end of the day—because everything is accounted for, not because you've stopped caring.


I hope, honestly, that when you see the new site, you let out a literal sigh.


Because if I can't buy you a massage, and I can't offer you a one-minute meditation (THERE ARE MEETINGS TO GO TO), the smallest thing we can give you is a tool that lets you get back to controlling the chaos, shipping good content, and resting easy knowing that everything is, finally, in your hands.
